name: Grammar And Clarity Best Practices
description: This module captures the best practices for grammar and clarity, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.
content:
This module captures the best practices for grammar and clarity, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When grammar and clarity decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
2. Re-check edge cases relevant to grammar and clarity (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
3. Document any non-obvious grammar and clarity decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
4. State assumptions about grammar and clarity explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
5. When grammar and clarity guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
6. Prefer the simplest grammar and clarity approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
7. Before starting grammar and clarity work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new grammar and clarity abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated grammar and clarity concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop grammar and clarity edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about grammar and clarity over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
